checksWhetherYourCountryHasCompleted: Checks whether your country has completed the focus with the given ID. Most used for event triggers, decision visibility, and as a prerequisite for later focuses. FOCUS_ID must point to a focus defined in this mod or vanilla; a typo won't error but will always return false. Commonly paired with date > 1940.1.1 to bound the time window.
requiresYourCountryToBeIn: Requires your country to be in no war at all (including small border conflicts). Often gates large focuses/decisions — to stop the player switching major paths mid-war. A truce doesn't count as 'not at war'; it returns yes only once all wars end. Different from has_civil_war — civil war is queried separately.
requiresYourCountryToBeIn_2: Requires your country to be in at least one war. Common as the trigger for wartime emergency events/decisions (war-industry mobilization, conscription drives). To filter 'at war with a specific country' use has_war_with = TAG for precision. Usually combined with war_support / manpower conditions to form a 'wartime' chain.
requiresYourCountryToNotBe: Requires your country to not be in a civil war. HOI4 civil wars are triggered by the start_civil_war effect (host vs breakaway faction) and are independent of has_war — having a civil war but no foreign war is entirely possible. Often used in focus chains as a 'only during a stable period' prerequisite. Returns no automatically once the civil war ends.
checksTheCurrentInGameDate: Checks the current in-game date. Format yyyy.m.d, supports > / < / =. Most used to control the timing of historical events/focuses — e.g. 'can't research the atom bomb before 1940'. The 1936 start counts from 1936.1.1; the 1939 scenario start must be accounted for before a date check. No range syntax — for a range, nest two date checks under AND.
checksYourCountrysStabilityStabilityAffe: Checks your country's stability (0.0~1.0). Stability affects factory output, political support, and event probability. Typical magnitudes: ~60-70% at start, 20-40% in war; focuses/decisions can grant +5%~15%. As a condition: > 0.5 median, > 0.7 high, < 0.3 turbulent. Compare with a decimal (0.5), not a percentage (50).
checksYourCountrysWarSupportDetermines: Checks your country's war support (0.0~1.0). Determines whether you can conscript, use total-mobilization laws, wage unrestricted submarine warfare, etc. Low in peacetime (20-40%), spikes after major events / being attacked. Common thresholds: > 0.3 (puppet expedition) / > 0.5 (full conscription) / > 0.7 (total mobilization). Use a decimal.
checksWhetherYourCountryHoldsA: Checks whether your country holds a custom flag. A flag is a boolean state marker set by the author via set_country_flag, carrying 'X happened' across events/decisions/focuses. Often used to unlock a follow-up path after some event. Extended form: has_country_flag = { flag = X date > 30 } (held for at least 30 days). Clear with clr_country_flag.
checksYourCountrysRulingPartysMain: Checks your country's ruling party's main ideology. Valid values: democratic / fascism / communism / neutrality. Note it's the 'ruling party', not the 'most-supported party' — it only changes when set_politics changes ruling_party. Sub-ideologies (social_liberal / stalinism) aren't checked here; use has_government_sub_ideology or has_idea.
checksACountrysSupportForA: Checks a country's support for a given ideology (0.0~1.0). Valid forms: democratic / fascism / communism / neutrality. Different from has_government (ruling party) — support can be high without being in power. Often used as a prerequisite for taking power via a legal election (> 0.5) or a civil war erupting (opposition crosses a threshold).
checksWhetherYourCountryIsA: Checks whether your country is a puppet of any country (any autonomy level: colony, integrated puppet, political proxy, etc.). The check is very loose — any subordinate relationship counts. To filter a specific overlord use is_subject_of = TAG; for a specific autonomy use has_autonomy_state = autonomy_X. Often used for 'independence-war events only a puppet can trigger'.
requiresYourCountryToNotBe_2: Requires your country to not be a puppet (fully independent). The strict opposite of is_puppet = yes. Often a base gate for 'only sovereign states can join factions / declare war / use diplomacy' — HOI4 disables many diplomatic/military effects for puppets. Combine with has_war_with to filter 'independent sovereign + currently at war'.
checksWhetherYourCountryActuallyControls: Checks whether your country actually controls the given state (not just owns it on paper — it must be garrisoned with no foreign occupation). STATE_ID is a number (not a TAG, not a province ID). Often used for 'hold/retake a key state' story triggers. Distinction: owns_state (legal ownership) vs controls_state (actual control). When occupied in war, owns still belongs to the original country, controls switches to the occupier.
checksYourCountrysAvailableManpowerPool: Checks your country's available manpower pool (recruited-but-not-deployed reserves) — not total population, not army size — the 'ready for the front line' number. Typical for a great power at start 50K-200K, 1M+ in total war. Common: > 100K (a mid-size country launches a campaign) / > 500K (can fight a protracted war). Check exhaustion with < 0.
blockTriggerChecksTheNumberOf: Block trigger: checks the number of division-level units. Sub-fields: size (count, supports > / < / =), type (optional, filter a unit type like infantry / armor / motorized), archetype (filter an equipment category). Without type it counts all divisions. Often used for 'have enough troops to deploy abroad'. Equivalent to num_divisions but more flexible. A full division ≈ 10K men.
aScopeControlClauseInvertsThe: A scope-control clause — inverts the result of its inner conditions. If any sub-condition inside the NOT block is true, the whole NOT is false. Common pitfall: NOT = { A B } is NOT(A AND B) — it passes if either A or B is false. For 'neither holds' use NOT = { OR = { A B } }. When deeply nested, consider extracting a scripted_trigger for readability.
aScopeControlClauseTheWhole: A scope-control clause — the whole OR is true when any sub-condition in the block is true. Most used for multiple-path prerequisites (completing focus A or B both activate what follows) or fallback conditions. Companions: AND (implicit by default; an outer brace is equivalent), NOT (inverts), count_triggers (require N met). Watch indentation when nesting; large mods wrap chains in a scripted_trigger.
aScopeChangeSwitchesTheCondition: A scope change: switches the condition scope to the given TAG country, querying that country's state inside. TAG can be a 3-letter country code (USA / GER / SOV) or a scope var (FROM / ROOT / PREV / event_target). Common uses: check whether an ally has joined the war, or an enemy's government type. FROM in an effect chain means 'the triggerer', ROOT is the 'outermost scope'. Put exists = yes first to avoid accessing a non-existent TAG.
queriesANumericVariableSetBy: Queries a numeric variable set by set_variable. Full syntax { var = NAME value = N compare = OP }, also short forms { NAME > N } / { NAME < N } / { NAME = N }. Valid compare values: less_than / less_than_or_equals / equals / greater_than_or_equals / greater_than / not_equals. Can compare two variables (put another variable name in the value field). Often used for mission/decision progress checks.
queriesAStateLevelBooleanMarker: Queries a state-level boolean marker within a state scope. Same mechanism as has_country_flag but on a state rather than a country. Used with set_state_flag / clr_state_flag. Common uses: state-level mission progress (has a state finished surveying) / regional story markers. State-scope switch: `every_owned_state = { limit = { has_state_flag = X } ... }`.
withinAStateScopeQueriesWhether: Within a state scope, queries whether the state is fully held by the TAG (legal ownership + actual occupation + no enemy cores). Distinct from owns_state (legal only, may not control) / controls_state (actual occupation, may not own). The strictest 'fully ours' check. Often used for mission conditions like 'all my core states are mine'. The target can be ROOT / FROM / TAG.
queriesWhetherTheUserHasThe: Queries whether the user has the given DLC enabled. The value is the DLC's full English name (in double quotes, case-sensitive). Common DLC names: 'Together for Victory' / 'Death or Dishonor' / 'Waking the Tiger' / 'Man the Guns' / 'La Resistance' / 'Battle for the Bosporus' / 'No Step Back' / 'By Blood Alone' / 'Arms Against Tyranny' / 'Trial of Allegiance' / 'Götterdämmerung'. Often used as a fallback for content only available with a DLC.
triggerTrueIfAnyOneOwned: Trigger: true if any one owned state of your country meets the inner conditions. It's a trigger (condition), not an effect (to execute → use random_owned_state). Companion all_owned_state (all must match). Same family: any_controlled_state / any_state (any on the whole map) / any_neighbor_country. Often used for gates like 'is there any coastal state where I can build a port'.
